Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the immediate next steps so we're all aligned.

Pain points you shared:
- Monthly inference spend has grown faster than expected due to many short-turn chats and high concurrency on peak hours.
- Current UX requires low tail latency (p95 <100ms) for interactive agents but cost is becoming the gating factor for expansion.
- Desire to keep data in the US region and maintain auditability for billing/usage reporting.

Goals we agreed on:
- Reduce inference spend while preserving the interactive experience (target: <= $50k/month budget constraint).
- Pilot in prod-like traffic by end of Q3, then expand if economics meet the target.
- Evaluate model variants + batching/caching levers to hit ROI targets.

High-level TCO assumptions we discussed (shared baseline for the attached spreadsheet):
- Current usage: ~100M tokens/month (chat + system tokens) -> estimated current cost: $85k/month (infra + model pricing).
- Target: move to ~$50k/month through a combination of batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantized model variants for lower-criticality paths.

Levers and impact (initial estimates):
- Intelligent batching (frontend + server coalescing): ~15-25% savings by increasing avg tokens/dispatch and reducing per-request overhead.
- Prefix/KV caching for common prompts and system messages: ~10-30% savings depending on prompt reuse.
- Model routing & quantization (e.g., q2/q4 variants for background completions): ~15-35% savings on routed traffic with a small quality delta.
- Region & spot capacity routing for non-latency-sensitive jobs: ~5-10% additional savings.

Next steps (agreed):
1) I'm sharing an initial TCO workbook (attached) with the assumptions above — Rafael will follow up with more detailed unit economics.
2) Please confirm the $50k/month hard budget and any constraints on pilot timing/regions.
3) Schedule a 30–45 min follow-up with your infra team (Rafael to join) to validate traffic patterns and constraints.

Attachments: ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx (worksheet with baseline & lever scenarios)

Thanks — happy to iterate on the assumptions.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical follow-up with more concrete unit economics and risk notes.

Assumptions:
- Avg request tokens (user + assistant + system): 75 tokens/request.
- Traffic profile: 40% interactive chat, 60% background/async workloads.
- Baseline cost estimate (model + infra): $0.85 per 1k tokens (example blended rate).

Basic math: 100M tokens/month -> 100,000 * $0.85 = $85,000/month (matches the deck).

Estimated savings by lever (order-of-magnitude):
- Batching (continuous coalescing + frontend batching): if we increase avg tokens/dispatch by 30% and reduce per-request overhead, effective cost reduction ~20% (reduces infra overhead & RPCs).
- Prefix/KV caching: with a 25% cache hit on typical prompts, save ~25% of token processing on cached flows (actual depends on prompt reuse).
- Quantized model routing: move 35% of non-critical completions to a q4_0/routed variant; model cost delta could be ~30% cheaper for routed traffic.
- Combined effect: multiplicative benefits; conservative combined savings estimate 40-45% -> gets you near $47–51k/month from the $85k baseline.

Operational notes / risks:
- Caching increases complexity around prompt variants; canonicalizing prompts improves hit rate but requires product changes.
- Batching effectiveness depends on burstiness; we can set latency SLOs and fall back to lower batching windows during peaks.
- Quantized models can introduce subtle quality regressions for certain prompts; recommend an A/B test for quality metrics during pilot.

Pilot deliverables (what I’ll prepare):
- Pilot config YAML with batching windows, cache TTLs, and routing rules.
- Costed estimate workbook by traffic segment (I’ll update the attached ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx).
- Lightweight A/B plan and eval prompts to monitor quality impact.

I’ll aim to have these materials ready prior to the follow-up—tentative ETA: end of day Fri 7/17.

Thanks,
